description:
Scenario: The trait methods create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>, update_object, destroy_object are generic over O, but the spec defines only one object type (Metadata). The MemoryBackend.create_object at memory.rs:702 does 'if O::TYPE_NAME == Metadata::TYPE_NAME' to gate the uniqueness check. If O != Metadata, the function happily creates a record without uniqueness enforcement.

Maintenance consequence:
(a) Any future caller (test fixture, future spec extension) that passes O != Metadata silently bypasses the §3.1 uniqueness constraint. The trait doc invariant requires backends to support Metadata's TYPE_NAME but does not constrain what backends should do for non-Metadata O values.

(b) Future readers of memory.rs see 'if O::TYPE_NAME == Metadata::TYPE_NAME' as an idiom and may conclude the generic-over-O shape is intentional polyphormism for multiple object types — leading them to invest in 'making MetadataBackend more generic' when the actual spec scope is single-object.

(c) supports_type<O>() at memory.rs:908 returns 'O::TYPE_NAME == Metadata::TYPE_NAME' — but the trait methods do not consult supports_type before doing work. So a caller that passes O != Metadata gets partial work done (state bumped, change log entry pushed) before any error surfaces from the type-keyed objects map.

Fix direction: either
(i) Drop the O generic from MetadataBackend method signatures (Metadata-specific trait — matches the spec's single-object reality). This is a breaking change to the trait.
(ii) Keep the generic but add a TYPE_NAME guard at the top of every method body, returning a clearly-marked error for non-Metadata O. Document the invariant prominently.

The canonical mail-server uses the same generic-over-O shape (backend.rs:91+) and has the same shape concern for object types it doesn't handle. So this is a workspace-wide pattern that metadata inherited — not a metadata-specific bug. But the maintainer-burden risk is real: it's a future-bug magnet for the worst kind of bug (silent state corruption with no error path).
title: MetadataBackend trait is generic over O: SetObject but only Metadata is supported — every create_object/update_object/destroy_object call must runtime-discriminate on O::TYPE_NAME
